briefings.title: Do You Trust Apple? | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Apple’s new HomeView smart home ecosystem and hardware lineup highlight a fundamental question of consumer trust, balancing the company's strengths in privacy and seamless second-party integrations against historical product abandonments and lagging AI performance.

briefings.title: Apple and a Hacker’s Future | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Ben Thompson’s Mac Mini was recently hacked via a zero-day screen sharing vulnerability, leading him to rely on an AI agent (Claude) to root out the malware; this incident, combined with frustrating TCC permission prompts and Apple's tightening restrictions on full-disk access, has made him envision a future where he no longer purchases Apple products by default.

briefings.title: Apps, Agents, and Aggregation | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: AI agents are shifting the technology paradigm from managing fixed apps and UIs to delegating tasks to autonomous agents equipped with dedicated cloud computers and generative UIs.

briefings.title: Frontier Overhangs | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Ben Thompson argues that calls from Anthropic's Dario Amodei and others to "pace the frontier" of AI under the guise of safetyism conveniently mask four major business overhangs—capability, pricing, capital, and safety—facing frontier labs.

briefings.title: Write Things Down | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Ben Thompson explores how writing things down—from David Allen's Getting Things Done methodology to markdown files used by AI models and agents—serves as the foundational mechanism for expanding human and artificial intelligence, arguing that while AI can simulate memory and workflows, true volition and moral intent remain uniquely human.

briefings.title: Autonomy and Innovation | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: AI agent capabilities have reached a point where fully automated offense is a reality, creating a critical asymmetry where attackers operate at machine speed while defensive companies stubbornly keep risk-averse humans in the loop.

briefings.title: Nvidia's Risky Business | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Big Tech is leaning on unprecedented debt, equity, and private-market financing—mirroring the 1870s railroad boom—to fund an estimated $600 billion in 2026 AI infrastructure.

briefings.title: What Happens When the AI Boom Runs Out of Money
briefings.tldr: Ben Thompson and the host discuss the economics, geopolitics, and business models of the AI boom, highlighting capital duration mismatches, the commoditization of compute, and how hyperscalers like Amazon and Google are positioned to challenge Nvidia and legacy incumbents.

briefings.title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Models? | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Reactions to Chinese open-weights AI models like Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 and Alibaba's Qwen 3.8B Max are overblown economically, but highlight real U.S. policy blunders regarding distillation and cybersecurity defense.

briefings.title: A Script for Mark Zuckerberg | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Meta is pivoting its strategic narrative to embrace its identity as an advertising and entertainment powerhouse, justifying massive AI CapEx by treating compute as a rentable asset that establishes a strict internal "hurdle rate" for ROI.

briefings.title: Anthropic’s Safety Superpower | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Anthropic’s recent clash with the U.S. government over its "Fable" model highlights a deeper strategic shift where the company leverages "safety" to justify aggressive data harvesting, silent model degradation, and a play to control the user touchpoint at the expense of traditional software competitors.

briefings.title: The iPhone’s Last Stand | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: While Microsoft’s "Project Solara" envisions a cloud-agent-driven, post-device ecosystem tailored for enterprise productivity, Apple’s revamped Siri AI doubles down on the iPhone as the central hub of personal context, betting that consumer-focused, interaction-driven AI is enough to secure its hardware dominance.

briefings.title: The Google Capital Company | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Google is raising $80 billion in equity—including a historic $10 billion partnership with Berkshire Hathaway—to fund its massive artificial intelligence infrastructure.

briefings.title: The SpaceX IPO and Data Centers in Space | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: SpaceX’s highly speculative $2 trillion IPO valuation is driven by Elon Musk's unique ability to convert narrative-driven capital into physical infrastructure, positioning the company to bypass Earth-bound data center zoning and power constraints by deploying laser-interconnected satellite "racks" in space optimized for the massive future market of agentic AI inference.

briefings.title: The Inference Shift | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: The AI hardware market is shifting from a GPU-centric model focused on training to a heterogeneous landscape where "Agentic Inference"—autonomous tasks performed without human oversight—prioritizes massive memory capacity and low cost over raw processing speed.

briefings.title: Amazon's Durability | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Amazon’s long-term strategy of building internal "primitives"—from logistics and custom silicon to satellite networks—and later selling them as third-party services creates a structural cost advantage and a durable moat that is increasingly well-positioned for the AI inference market.

briefings.title: Tim Cook’s Impeccable Timing | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Tim Cook’s 15-year tenure as Apple CEO transitioned the company from a "zero-to-one" innovator under Steve Jobs to a "1-to-n" operational juggernaut, increasing Apple's valuation from $297 billion to $4 trillion while leaving behind critical long-term questions regarding AI and China.

briefings.title: Mythos, Muse, and the Opportunity Cost of Compute | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: The era of "zero marginal costs" that defined the 2010s is ending as AI creates massive capital intensity and compute constraints, forcing tech giants to prioritize internal workloads over external customers based on opportunity costs rather than traditional supply/demand.

briefings.title: Apple’s 50 Years of Integration | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: As Apple reaches its 50th anniversary, its core strategy of hardware and software integration remains its greatest competitive advantage, allowing the company to aggregate third-party AI models and monetize them through its hardware moat rather than investing in costly infrastructure.

briefings.title: Agents Over Bubbles | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: The shift from simple chatbots to autonomous "agents" has transformed AI from a speculative bubble into a high-demand utility, justifying massive infrastructure spending through deep software integration and tangible enterprise productivity gains.

briefings.title: Anthropic and Alignment | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Anthropic’s refusal to allow the U.S. military to use its models for surveillance or autonomous weapons creates a fundamental conflict of sovereignty; if AI is as transformative as nuclear weapons, the U.S. government cannot tolerate a private corporation acting as an independent power base that dictates national security terms.

briefings.title: FULL INTERVIEW: Ben Thompson on Anthropic v. DoW
briefings.tldr: As AI evolves into a frontier source of national power, private labs like Anthropic must recognize that the "alignment" problem extends beyond ethics to the survival of the nation-state; the U.S. government will ultimately not tolerate private executives making unilateral decisions on matters of national security or surveillance.

briefings.title: The Memory Crowd-Out | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: AI is driving a structural shift back to the "thin client" computing model, where cloud-based inference and autonomous agents render local processing power secondary to connectivity.

briefings.title: Thin Is In | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: The rise of generative AI is driving a shift back to "thin client" computing where local hardware matters less than cloud connectivity, a transition being accelerated by an AI-driven global memory shortage that makes local devices more expensive and less essential.

briefings.title: Ben Thompson from Stratechery on AI ads, the end of SaaS, and the future of media
briefings.tldr: The internet economy is transitioning from seat-based SaaS and social networks to AI-mediated "agentic commerce," where the primary risks are a looming 2029 hardware bottleneck and a failure by Western regulators to recognize that algorithmic control, not data privacy, is the true center of geopolitical power.

briefings.title: Microsoft and Software Survival | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: Microsoft is navigating a fundamental shift where AI-written code commoditizes software, forcing a transition from "growing the pie" to a predatory battle for industry adjacencies.

briefings.title: TSMC Risk | Stratechery by Ben Thompson
briefings.tldr: TSMC's conservative investment strategy since late 2022 has created a significant bottleneck for the AI industry, leading to billions in foregone revenue for hyperscalers and threatening future growth, a problem only solvable by fostering strong competition in the foundry space.
